0.long_answer: Mutations in the Ras/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathways are known to cause a range of developmental anomalies that overlap with the clinical features observed in Fryns-Aftimos syndrome. In particular, abnormalities such as macrocephaly (an abnormally large head circumference), congenital heart defects, and distinctive anomalies of the digits (finger changes) are observed. These features mirror the presentation in Fryns-Aftimos syndrome, where patients may exhibit similar craniofacial overgrowth and digital dysmorphisms alongside heart malformations. Thus, the overlap in symptoms suggests a shared pathogenic mechanism related to disrupted developmental signaling in both conditions.
